A local relation body exists in the tracked registry and typed owner snapshot, while the separate b35 target's meaning/source is not established.

The two local regime rows are distinct and have their own effective starts.

The relation DTO carries schema_regime_id, scope_identity_refs, relation_provenance_ref, visibility_knowledge_from, and purpose_admission_from; it does not define an independent row-content reference.

canonical_row_hashes_from_r2152.conclusion: Neither the whole registry digest nor either local row digest equals b35. Both distinct rows reuse b35. A content hash proves the bytes hashed, not their issuer, authority, custody, or currentness.

alternatives.proposal: Reuse the already-owned typed relation rows as local relation content, but never equate their bytes/digests with b35. If the chosen source contract needs content-addressed local rows, add a distinct row-content reference or derive it from the canonical typed row under a versioned schema; retain relation_provenance_ref as a separate unresolved provenance edge until its meaning is supplied.
advantages: Uses the existing two-row owner registry and typed DTO; avoids a new provenance subsystem.
Makes local content identity and upstream provenance separate, testable concepts.
costs_and_migration: Requires a versioned DTO/resource/bridge migration and compatibility behavior for legacy v1 rows.
Legacy b35 remains unresolved; consumers cannot claim external provenance from local bytes.
alternatives.authority_and_time: The local row's source, authority, and admission times remain exactly those already supplied. They do not establish an external issuer or the validity/currentness interval of b35.
alternatives.status: Potentially closes the local artifact/bridge gap for a local relation claim after owner ratification and real producer→CAS→consumer verification; does not close external provenance or B31.

alternatives.proposal: Only if the responsible owner supplies the actual b35 artifact and contract, extend the existing resolver/verification bridge to bind exact bytes to a typed schema and the relation rows.
required_input: Versioned target schema and verifier/signature rule
Custody and any institutionally supplied validity/currentness and knowledge/admission times
Explicit binding to the one or more relation rows and scope
advantages: Preserves the current reference if it truly identifies a shared issuer statement.
Keeps external authority inputs distinct from locally recomputed row selection.
costs_and_migration: Cannot be implemented honestly from current inputs; must not synthesize issuer, law, custody, or currentness.
Existing and new rows remain fail-closed until matching evidence arrives.
alternatives.status: External claim remains not_established until authentic owner input and consumer verification exist.

alternatives.proposal: If the owner rules b35 to be legacy/unresolved or redundant, consolidate around the existing canonical owner registry/typed row as the local source of relation content, preserve b35 in historical input or explicit legacy provenance, and define a versioned migration.
advantages: Avoids an ungrounded second authority store and reduces duplicated row definitions.
Can make local source-of-truth and replay semantics explicit.
costs_and_migration: Requires owner ratification and explicit handling of existing hashes/history; no manifest or hash rewrite is allowed to make pairing pass.
Does not establish external provenance if no target exists.
alternatives.authority_and_time: Preserve the existing per-row visibility-knowledge and purpose-admission dates. Any distinct provenance validity/currentness must come from its issuer, not be inferred from local effective dates.
alternatives.status: Only local row composition may become admitted under a declared local contract; external provenance remains limited or unresolved as selected.

alternatives.proposal: Not recommended. Do not build a new issuer/provenance subsystem before the owner identifies the field meaning and provides authoritative inputs.
alternatives.reason: It would create a second authority surface without the source facts required to validate it and would violate reuse-first.

recommended_narrow_decision.proposal: Until the owner selects one of the meanings and supplies any required external artifact, preserve fail-closed behavior. If the owner selects local row content, use distinct local content identity and keep b35 semantically separate; do not silently reinterpret or rewrite b35.
recommended_narrow_decision.why: This is the smallest choice compatible with observed hashes, two distinct rows, existing source/API shapes, and the evidence boundary. It resolves ambiguity without making an external factual claim.
recommended_narrow_decision.choice_owner: G decision required with the L5 source/contract owner; named institution/issuer is not established in current evidence.

Keep b35 provenance separate unless authenticated semantics are provided.
implementation_and_falsifier.falsifier: Using genuine owner inputs, run both regime rows through producer→CAS→resolver→finalizer→denominator consumer. Then mutate or remove one row's content/ref/time while keeping schema/test markers and registry declarations; the actual consumer must refuse the changed/missing relation and the semantic test must turn red if the resolver/content-binding predicate is removed. Also prove one row cannot satisfy the sibling row's ref, scope, or time binding. No self-labeled artifact or synthetic empty result counts.
